headline: BCB optimistic Nahid Rana to be fit for Australia Test series
summary: The pace sensation suffered a side-strain during the T20I series in Zimbabwe, but selectors expect him to recover in time for the Darwin Test.
details: Nahid Rana suffered a side-strain during the second T20I against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo, forcing him to miss the series-deciding third match.
The pace bowler will undergo scans after returning to Bangladesh on Wednesday to determine the exact extent of the injury.
While initial reports suggested a recovery period of two to three weeks, the BCB selection panel remains optimistic about his availability for the first Test in Darwin on August 13.
Rana has become a key part of the pace attack, recently claiming four wickets in an opening ODI fixture against Australia at home.
Australia's coach Andrew McDonald has already identified Rana as a potential threat, noting his unique action and potency in Australian conditions.
In addition to Rana, T20I captain Litton Das is recovering from an injury in Singapore and will undergo scans on Wednesday before returning on July 25.
Shoriful Islam is also nursing an injury but is reportedly recovering well, with the selection panel awaiting medical reports before announcing the squad.
This upcoming series will mark Bangladesh's first Test tour of Australia in 23 years, facing a full-strength Australian squad featuring Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins.
caption:

headline_marked: 600 crore BDT [[agricultural loans waived for 7 lakh farmers]]
headline: 600 crore BDT agricultural loans waived for 7 lakh farmers
summary: Bangladesh Krishi Bank has implemented a significant portion of the government's loan waiver program to support small and marginal farmers.
details: The Bangladesh Krishi Bank (BKB) has waived agricultural loans totaling over 604 crore BDT for 700,967 farmers across 48 districts in the last five months.
This action follows a decision by the BNP government in February to waive agricultural loans, including interest, up to 10,000 BDT per farmer.
The overall government initiative aims to waive a total of 1,550 crore BDT, benefiting approximately 1.2 million farmers across the crop, fishery, and livestock sectors.
BKB alone has implemented approximately 39% of the total government-announced waiver, as the bank provides about 63% of the total agricultural loans distributed in the country.
The bank stated that unpaid loans had created significant financial and psychological pressure on marginal farmers due to natural disasters, rising production costs, and market instability.
Managing Director of BKB, Sanchia Binte Ali, noted that the waiver allows these farmers to be free from debt burdens and regain access to regular banking services and new loans for production.
The move aligns with the BNP's election manifesto, which included promises such as agricultural loan waivers, 'Family Cards', and 'Farmer Cards'.
Historically, a similar loan waiver of up to 5,000 BDT was implemented during Begum Khaleda Zia's tenure from 1991 to 1996.
caption:
Over 600 crore BDT in loans waived for 7 lakh farmers! 

Small and marginal farmers are getting a fresh start.

The Bangladesh Krishi Bank (BKB) has waived agricultural loans totaling over 604 crore BDT for 700,967 farmers across 48 districts in the last five months.

This action follows a decision by the BNP government in February to waive agricultural loans, including interest, up to 10,000 BDT per farmer.

The overall government initiative aims to waive a total of 1,550 crore BDT, benefiting approximately 1.2 million farmers across the crop, fishery, and livestock sectors.

BKB alone has implemented approximately 39% of the total government-announced waiver, as the bank provides about 63% of the total agricultural loans distributed in the country.

The bank stated that unpaid loans had created significant financial and psychological pressure on marginal farmers due to natural disasters, rising production costs, and market instability.

Managing Director of BKB, Sanchia Binte Ali, noted that the waiver allows these farmers to be free from debt burdens and regain access to regular banking services and new loans for production.

The move aligns with the BNP's election manifesto, which included promises such as agricultural loan waivers, 'Family Cards', and 'Farmer Cards'.

Historically, a similar loan waiver of up to 5,000 BDT was implemented during Begum Khaleda Zia's tenure from 1991 to 1996.
